title.zh: 卷二百九十八 列傳第一百八十六 隱逸
title.raw: 卷二百九十八 列傳第一百八十六 隱逸 Volume 298 Biographies 186: Recluses

sentences.zh: 張介福 倪瓚 徐舫 楊恆 陳洄 楊引 吳海 劉閔 楊黼 孫一元 沈周 陳繼儒

translations.literal: Zhang Jiefu, Ni Zan, Xu Fang, Yang Heng, Chen Hui, Yang Yin, Wu Hai, Liu Min, Yang Pu, Sun Yiyuan, Shen Zhou, Chen Jiru
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiefu, Ni Zan, Xu Fang, Yang Heng, Chen Hui, Yang Yin, Wu Hai, Liu Min, Yang Pu, Sun Yiyuan, Shen Zhou, and Chen Jiru

sentences.zh: 韓愈言：「《蹇》之六二曰『王臣蹇蹇』，而《蠱》之上九曰『高尚其事』，由所居之時不一，而所蹈之德不同。

translations.literal: Han Yu said: "The second line of the hexagram Jian says 'The king's minister, jian jian,' while the top line of the hexagram Gu says 'He elevates his undertaking' — because the times each occupies are not the same, and the virtue each practices is different."
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu wrote that the second line of the hexagram Jian reads, "The king's minister, steadfast in difficulty," while the top line of Gu reads, "He elevates his own course" — for the times in which one lives differ, and so do the virtues one follows.

sentences.zh: 」夫聖賢以用世為心，而逸民以肥遁為節 ，豈性分實然，亦各行其志而已。

translations.literal: Sages and worthies take serving the world as their heart's aim, while hermit-scholars take prosperous withdrawal as their standard — this is not because their innate natures are necessarily different; each simply follows his own resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Sages and worthies set their hearts on serving the world, while recluses take prosperous withdrawal as their code. This is not because their natures are utterly unlike; each simply pursues his own chosen path.

sentences.zh: 明太祖興禮儒士，聘文學，搜求岩穴，側席幽人，後置不為君用之罰，然韜跡自遠者，亦不乏人。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu of Ming honoured Confucian scholars, appointed literary men, searched caves and cliffs, and sat attentively awaiting recluses; later he imposed punishments on those who would not serve their ruler — yet those who hid their traces and kept their distance were never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor honoured Confucian scholars, recruited literary men, searched out hermits in mountain caves, and waited eagerly for recluses; later he punished those who refused to serve the throne — yet men who hid their tracks and kept aloof were never scarce.

sentences.zh: 迨中葉承平，聲教淪浹，巍科顯爵，頓天網以羅英俊，民之秀者，無不觀國光而賓王廷矣。

translations.literal: By the mid-dynasty, when peace reigned and culture spread throughout the land, great examination successes and lofty ranks cast the broad net of Heaven to gather talent; among the people's finest, none failed to gaze upon the nation's glory and come as guests to the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: By the mid-dynasty, in an age of peace when imperial teaching had permeated the realm, high examination honors and distinguished ranks cast Heaven's wide net to gather the talented; among the finest of the people, none failed to behold the nation's glory and present themselves at the royal court.

sentences.zh: 其抱瑰材，蘊積學，槁形泉石，絕意當世者，靡得而稱焉。

translations.literal: Those who cherished rare talent, stored up learning, wasted their forms among springs and stones, and severed all ties with the age — few could be named.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held rare gifts, amassed learning, wasted their bodies among springs and rocks, and turned their backs on the world could scarcely be named at all.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，世道升降之端，系所遭逢，豈非其時為之哉。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, the turning points in the rise and fall of the world's way depend on what one meets with in life — is it not truly the times that shape this?
translations.idiomatic: Seen in this light, whether the age rises or falls hinges on what one encounters in life — is it not the times themselves that make the difference?

sentences.zh: 凡徵聘所及，文學行誼可稱者，已散見諸傳。

translations.literal: All those reached by summons and appointment, whose learning and conduct were worthy of praise, have already been scattered through various biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Those reached by summons and appointment whose learning and conduct were commendable have already appeared in other biographies.

sentences.zh: 茲取貞節超邁者數人，作《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: Here several men of unwavering integrity and surpassing virtue are selected, to compose "The Biographies of Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: Here several men of steadfast integrity and extraordinary character are selected to compose the Biographies of Recluses.

sentences.zh: 張介福

translations.literal: Zhang Jiefu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiefu

sentences.zh: 張介福，字子祺，自懷慶徙吳中。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiefu, styled Ziqi, moved from Huaiqing to the Wu region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiefu, styled Ziqi, moved from Huaiqing to the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 少受學於許衡。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Xu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Xu Heng.

sentences.zh: 二親早終，遂無仕進意。

translations.literal: Both parents died early, and thereafter he had no mind to pursue office.
translations.idiomatic: Both his parents died early, and from then on he had no wish to enter official life.

sentences.zh: 家貧，冬不能具夾襦，或遺以糹寧絮，不受，纖介必以禮。

translations.literal: His family was poor; in winter he could not afford a lined robe. When someone offered him cotton wadding, he would not accept it; even the smallest gift he handled only according to propriety.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and in winter he could not afford a lined robe. When someone offered him cotton padding, he refused it; even the smallest gift he accepted only in accordance with propriety.

sentences.zh: 張士誠入吳，有卒犯其家，危坐不為起。

translations.literal: When Zhang Shicheng entered Wu, a soldier violated his household, but he sat upright and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shicheng entered Wu, a soldier broke into his home, but he sat upright and did not stand.

sentences.zh: 刀斫面，僕地，醒復取冠戴之，坐自若。

translations.literal: A blade slashed his face; he fell to the ground. When he came to, he took up his cap and put it on again, and sat as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: A blade cut his face and he fell to the ground. When he came to, he picked up his cap, put it on again, and sat as calmly as before.

sentences.zh: 卒怪，以為異物，走去。

translations.literal: The soldier, astonished, thought him something uncanny and ran off.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier, startled, took him for something uncanny and fled.

sentences.zh: 介福恐發其先墓，往廬焉。

translations.literal: Jiefu feared his ancestral graves would be violated, and went to dwell in a hut beside them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that his ancestors' graves would be desecrated, Jiefu went to live in a hut beside them.

sentences.zh: 士誠聞而欲致之，不可。

translations.literal: Shicheng heard of this and wished to summon him, but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng heard of this and wished to summon him, but could not.

sentences.zh: 使其弟往問，答曰：「無樂亂，無貪天禍，無忘國家。

translations.literal: He sent his younger brother to inquire; Jiefu replied: "Do not delight in disorder, do not greedily invite Heaven's calamity, do not forget the state."
translations.idiomatic: He sent his younger brother to inquire; Jiefu replied, "Do not take pleasure in disorder, do not greedily invite Heaven's punishment, and do not forget the state."

sentences.zh: 」饋之，力辭。

translations.literal: When gifts were sent, he firmly declined them.
translations.idiomatic: When gifts were sent to him, he firmly declined them.

sentences.zh: 已，病革，謂其友曰：「吾志希古人，未能也。

translations.literal: Later, when his illness became critical, he told his friends: "My ambition aspired to the ancients; I have not achieved it."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his illness became critical, he told his friends, "My ambition was to emulate the ancients, but I have not done so."

sentences.zh: 惟無污於時，庶幾哉。

translations.literal: Only that I have not been sullied by the times — perhaps that much can be said.
translations.idiomatic: Only that I have not been stained by the age — perhaps that much may be said.

sentences.zh: 」遂卒。

translations.literal: Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died.

sentences.zh: 倪瓚，字元鎮，無錫人也。

translations.literal: Ni Zan, styled Yuanzhen, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Zan, styled Yuanzhen, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 家雄於貲，工詩，善書畫。

translations.literal: His family was wealthy, he was skilled at poetry, and excelled at calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: His family was extremely wealthy; he was accomplished in poetry and excelled at calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 四方名士日至其門。

translations.literal: Renowned men from all quarters came daily to his door.
translations.idiomatic: Distinguished men from all directions came to his door every day.

sentences.zh: 所居有閣曰清閟，幽迥絕塵。

translations.literal: At his residence was a pavilion called Qingbi, secluded, remote, and free of worldly dust.
translations.idiomatic: At his residence stood a pavilion called the Pure and Secluded, remote and utterly removed from the dust of the world.

sentences.zh: 藏書數千卷，皆手自勘定。

translations.literal: He kept several thousand volumes of books, all collated by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He kept several thousand volumes in his library, every one collated by his own hand.

sentences.zh: 古鼎法書，名琴奇畫，陳列左右。

translations.literal: Ancient tripods, model calligraphy, famous zithers, and extraordinary paintings were displayed all around.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient bronzes, master calligraphy, famous zithers, and rare paintings were displayed on every side.

sentences.zh: 四時卉木，縈繞其外，高木修篁，蔚然深秀，故自號雲林居士。

translations.literal: Seasonal flowers and trees encircled it outside; tall trees and slender bamboos stood lush and deeply elegant, so he styled himself the Cloud-Forest Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Flowering plants of every season encircled it outside, and tall trees and slender bamboos rose in luxuriant, deep beauty; hence he styled himself the Cloud-Forest Recluse.

sentences.zh: 時與客觴詠其中。

translations.literal: From time to time he shared wine and poetry with guests there.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he shared wine and verse with guests there.

sentences.zh: 為人有潔癖，盥濯不離手。

translations.literal: By nature he had a fastidious love of cleanliness; washing never left his hands.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was fastidiously clean; he washed his hands constantly.

sentences.zh: 俗客造廬，比去，必洗滌其處。

translations.literal: When vulgar guests visited his dwelling, as soon as they left he would wash the place where they had been.
translations.idiomatic: When common guests visited his home, he always washed the place where they had sat as soon as they left.

sentences.zh: 求縑素者踵至，瓚亦時應之。

translations.literal: Those seeking silk for painting came one after another, and Zan also responded from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Those seeking silk scrolls for painting came in an endless stream, and Zan would sometimes oblige them.

sentences.zh: 至正初，海內無事，忽散其貲給親故，人咸怪之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhizheng era, when the realm was at peace, he suddenly dispersed his wealth among relatives and friends; everyone thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhizheng era, when the realm was at peace, he suddenly gave away his fortune to relatives and friends, and everyone thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 未幾兵興，富家悉被禍，而瓚扁舟箬笠，往來震澤、三泖間，獨不罹患。

translations.literal: Before long warfare arose; wealthy families all suffered disaster, while Zan, in a small boat with bamboo hat, moved between Lake Zhen and the Three Marshes, alone untouched by calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Before long war broke out, and wealthy families all met with disaster; but Zan, in a small boat with a bamboo hat, traveled between Lake Zhen and the Three Marshes and alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 張士誠累欲鉤致之，逃漁舟以免。

translations.literal: Zhang Shicheng repeatedly wished to lure him in, but he escaped by hiding in a fishing boat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shicheng repeatedly tried to lure him in, but he escaped by hiding aboard a fishing boat.

sentences.zh: 其弟士信以幣乞畫，瓚又斥去。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shixin sent gifts to beg for a painting, and Zan drove him away again.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shixin sent gifts to request a painting, and Zan drove him away once more.

sentences.zh: 士信恚，他日從賓客游湖上，聞異香出葭葦間，疑為瓚也，物色漁舟中，果得之。

translations.literal: Shixin, enraged, one day went boating on the lake with guests. He caught a strange fragrance from among the reeds, suspected it was Zan, searched the fishing boats, and indeed found him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin, furious, went boating on the lake one day with his guests. Catching a strange fragrance from among the reeds, he suspected it was Zan, searched the fishing boats, and found him.

sentences.zh: 抶幾斃，終無一言。

translations.literal: He was beaten nearly to death, yet never uttered a word.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten nearly to death, yet never said a word.

sentences.zh: 及吳平，瓚年老矣，黃冠野服，混跡編氓。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, Zan was already old; in Daoist cap and rustic dress he mingled among common folk.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu was pacified, Zan was already old; wearing a Daoist cap and rustic clothes, he blended in among the common people.

sentences.zh: 洪武七年卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Hongwu, at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Hongwu, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 徐舫，字方舟，桐廬人。

translations.literal: Xu Fang, styled Fangzhou, was a native of Tonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fang, styled Fangzhou, was a native of Tonglu.

sentences.zh: 幼輕俠，好擊劍、走馬、蹴踘。

translations.literal: In youth he was reckless and chivalric, fond of swordplay, horsemanship, and cuju.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was reckless and chivalric, fond of swordplay, horsemanship, and cuju.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，習科舉業。

translations.literal: Later he regretted this and took up examination studies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he regretted this and turned to examination studies.

sentences.zh: 已，復棄去，學為歌詩。

translations.literal: Then he abandoned that too and learned to compose songs and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Then he abandoned that as well and devoted himself to song and poetry.

sentences.zh: 睦故多詩人，唐有方干、徐凝、李頻、施肩吾，宋有高師魯、滕元秀，號睦州詩派，舫悉取步聚之。

translations.literal: Mu prefecture had long produced many poets: in Tang there were Fang Gan, Xu Ning, Li Pin, and Shi Jianwu; in Song there were Gao Shilu and Teng Yuanxiu — called the Muzhou school of poetry — and Fang took them all as models to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Mu prefecture had long produced many poets: in Tang, Fang Gan, Xu Ning, Li Pin, and Shi Jianwu; in Song, Gao Shilu and Teng Yuanxiu — known as the Muzhou school — and Fang took them all as models.

sentences.zh: 既乃游四方，交其名士，詩益工。

translations.literal: Then he traveled the four quarters, befriended eminent men, and his poetry grew ever finer.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled widely, befriended distinguished men, and his poetry grew ever finer.

sentences.zh: 行省參政蘇天爵將薦之，舫笑曰：「吾詩人耳，可羈以章紱哉。

translations.literal: Su Tianjue, provincial administration commissioner, was about to recommend him. Fang laughed and said: "I am but a poet — can I be bound with official seals and ribbons?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Tianjue, provincial administration commissioner, was about to recommend him. Fang laughed and said, "I am only a poet — can I be bound with official seals and ribbons?"

sentences.zh: 」竟避去。

translations.literal: In the end he avoided it and left.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he avoided the offer and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 築室江皋，日苦吟於雲煙出沒間，翛然若與世隔，因自號滄江散人。

translations.literal: He built a dwelling on the riverbank and daily toiled at verse amid rising and vanishing mist, detached as if cut off from the world, and styled himself the Unbound Man of the Dark River.
translations.idiomatic: He built a house on the riverbank and spent his days composing verse amid drifting mist, detached as if cut off from the world, and styled himself the Unbound Man of the Dark River.

sentences.zh: 宋濂、劉基、葉琛、章溢之赴召也，舟溯桐江，忽有人黃冠鹿裘立江上，招基而笑，且語侵之。

translations.literal: When Song Lian, Liu Ji, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi were going to answer the imperial summons, their boat went up the Tong River. Suddenly a man in yellow cap and deerskin robe stood on the riverbank, beckoned to Ji and laughed, and spoke to him with mockery.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Lian, Liu Ji, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi were traveling to answer the imperial summons, their boat went up the Tong River. Suddenly a man in a yellow cap and deerskin robe stood on the bank, beckoned to Ji with a laugh, and spoke to him in mockery.

sentences.zh: 基望見，急延入舟中。

translations.literal: Ji saw him and hastily invited him into the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji saw him and quickly invited him aboard.

sentences.zh: 琛、溢競歡謔，各取冠服服之，欲載上黟川，其人不可乃止。

translations.literal: Chen and Yi vied in merry banter, each took cap and robe and dressed outside them on him, wishing to carry him up to Yichuan, but the man would not agree and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and Yi vied in merry banter, each took cap and robe and dressed him in them, wishing to carry him up to Yichuan, but the man would not agree and they desisted.

sentences.zh: 濂初未相識，以問。

translations.literal: Lian did not know him at first and asked.
translations.idiomatic: Lian did not know him at first and asked who he was.

sentences.zh: 基曰：「此徐方舟也。

translations.literal: Ji said: "This is Xu Fangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "This is Xu Fangzhou."

sentences.zh: 」濂因起共歡笑，酌酒而別。

translations.literal: Lian then rose and shared laughter with them, poured wine, and parted.
translations.idiomatic: Lian then rose and joined in their laughter, poured wine, and took his leave.

sentences.zh: 舫詩有《瑤林》、《滄江》二集。

translations.literal: Fang's poetry includes two collections, Yaolin and Cangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's poetry survives in two collections, Yaolin and Cangjiang.

sentences.zh: 年六十八，丙午春，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the age of sixty-eight, in the spring of the bingwu year, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of sixty-eight, in the spring of the bingwu year, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 楊恆，字本初，諸暨人。

translations.literal: Yang Heng, styled Benchu, was a native of Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Heng, styled Benchu, was a native of Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 外族方氏建義塾，館四方游學士，恆幼往受諸經，輒領其旨要。

translations.literal: His maternal clan, the Fang family, built a charity school and housed traveling scholars from all quarters. Heng went there in youth to study the classics and always grasped their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal clan, the Fang family, built a charity school and housed traveling scholars from all quarters. As a boy Heng went there to study the classics and always grasped their essential meaning.

sentences.zh: 文峻潔，有聲郡邑間。

translations.literal: His writing was severe and pure, and he had a reputation throughout the district and county.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was austere and polished, and he was known throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 浦江鄭氏延為師，閱十年退居白鹿山，戴棕冠，披羊裘，帶經耕煙雨間，嘯歌自樂，因自號白鹿生。

translations.literal: The Zheng family of Pujiang invited him as teacher. After ten years he retired to Mount Bailu, wore a palm-fiber cap and sheepskin coat, farmed with classics in hand amid mist and rain, sang and rejoiced by himself, and styled himself the Bailu Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng family of Pujiang engaged him as a teacher. After ten years he retired to Mount Bailu, wore a palm-fiber cap and sheepskin coat, farmed with the classics in hand amid mist and rain, sang to amuse himself, and styled himself the Bailu Recluse.

sentences.zh: 太祖既下浙東，命欒鳳知州事。

translations.literal: After the Founder had taken eastern Zhejiang, he appointed Luan Feng to administer the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hongwu Emperor had taken eastern Zhejiang, he appointed Luan Feng to administer the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鳳請為州學師，恆固讓不起。

translations.literal: Feng requested him to serve as teacher of the prefectural school, but Heng firmly declined and would not rise to office.
translations.idiomatic: Feng asked him to serve as teacher of the prefectural school, but Heng firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 鳳乃命州中子弟即家問道。

translations.literal: Feng then ordered the young men of the prefecture to seek the Way at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Feng then had the young men of the prefecture come to his home to study with him.

sentences.zh: 政有缺失，輒貽書咨訪。

translations.literal: When there were faults in governance, Feng would send letters to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: When there were faults in governance, Feng would write to consult him.

sentences.zh: 後唐鐸知紹興，欲辟起之，復固辭。

translations.literal: Later Tang Duo governed Shaoxing and wished to summon him to office, but he again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tang Duo governed Shaoxing and wished to summon him to office, he again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 宋濂之為學士也，擬薦為國子師，聞不受州郡辟命，乃已。

translations.literal: When Song Lian became a Hanlin academician, he planned to recommend Heng as teacher of the National University, but hearing that he would not accept appointments from prefectures and districts, he dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Lian became a Hanlin academician, he planned to recommend Heng as teacher of the National University, but hearing that he would not accept appointments from prefectures and districts, he dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 恆性醇篤，與人語，出肺肝相示。

translations.literal: Heng's nature was sincere and steadfast; in speaking with others he showed his innermost heart and liver.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was sincere and steadfast by nature; in conversation he spoke from the heart without reserve.

sentences.zh: 事稍乖名義，輒峻言指斥。

translations.literal: When matters slightly violated right principle, he would sternly speak out in rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: When anything fell short of right principle, he would speak out sternly in rebuke.

sentences.zh: 家無儋石，而臨財甚介，鄉人奉為楷法焉。

translations.literal: His household had not even a dan of grain, yet in facing wealth he was extremely scrupulous; the people of his district took him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: His household had scarcely a bushel of grain, yet he was extremely scrupulous in matters of money; the people of his district took him as a model.

sentences.zh: 時有陳洄者，義烏人。

translations.literal: At the time there was one Chen Hui, a native of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was one Chen Hui, a native of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 幼治經，長通百家言。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the classics; grown, he mastered the teachings of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied the classics; as an adult he mastered the teachings of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 初欲以功名顯，既而隱居，戴青霞冠，披白鹿裘，不復與塵事接。

translations.literal: At first he wished to achieve fame through official success, but later he went into seclusion, wore a green-cloud cap and white-deer fur coat, and no longer had dealings with worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At first he wished to achieve fame through official success, but later he went into seclusion, wore a green-cloud cap and white-deer fur coat, and no longer had dealings with worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 所居近大溪，多修竹，自號竹溪逸民。

translations.literal: His dwelling was near a great stream, with many tall bamboos; he styled himself the Bamboo-Stream Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling lay near a great stream amid many tall bamboos, and he styled himself the Bamboo-Stream Recluse.

sentences.zh: 常乘小艇，吹短簫，吹已，叩舷而歌，悠然自適。

translations.literal: He often rode a small boat, played a short flute, and when finished, struck the gunwale and sang, at ease and content.
translations.idiomatic: He often rode in a small boat, played a short flute, and when he finished, struck the gunwale and sang, perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 宋濂俱為之傳。

translations.literal: Song Lian wrote biographies for both of them.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lian wrote biographies for both Yang Heng and Chen Hui.

sentences.zh: 楊引，吉水人。

translations.literal: Yang Yin, a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin was a native of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 好學能詩文，為宋濂、陶安所稱。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled in poetry and prose; he was praised by Song Lian and Tao An.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was accomplished in poetry and prose; Song Lian and Tao An praised him.

sentences.zh: 駙馬都尉陸賢從受學，入朝，舉止端雅。

translations.literal: The imperial son-in-law Lu Xian studied under him; when he entered court, his bearing was dignified and refined.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son-in-law Lu Xian studied under him; when Lu entered court, his bearing was dignified and refined.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，問誰教者，賢以引對，立召見，賜食。

translations.literal: The Founder was pleased and asked who had taught him. Xian named Yin, who was immediately summoned, received an audience, and was granted food.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwu Emperor was pleased and asked who had taught him. Xian named Yin, who was immediately summoned, received an audience, and was granted a meal.

sentences.zh: 他日，賢以褻服見，引太息曰：「是其心易我，不可久居此矣。

translations.literal: Another day Xian came to see him in informal dress. Yin sighed deeply and said: "His heart has changed toward me; I cannot remain here long."
translations.idiomatic: One day Xian came to see him in informal dress. Yin sighed deeply and said, "His heart has changed toward me; I cannot stay here much longer."

sentences.zh: 」復以纂修征，亦不就。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned for compilation work, but again would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to join a compilation project, but again declined.

sentences.zh: 其教學者，先操履而後文藝。

translations.literal: In teaching students, he put conduct first and literary skill afterward.
translations.idiomatic: In teaching students, he put conduct first and literary skill second.

sentences.zh: 嘗揭《論語鄉黨》篇示人曰：「吾教自有養生術，安事偃仰吐納為。

translations.literal: He once displayed the Xiangdang chapter of the Analects to others and said: "My teaching has its own art of nurturing life — what need is there for breathing exercises of lying and rising?"
translations.idiomatic: He once displayed the Xiangdang chapter of the Analects to others and said, "My teaching has its own art of nurturing life — what need is there for breathing exercises?"

sentences.zh: 」乃節飲食，時動息，迄老視聽不衰。

translations.literal: He then regulated his diet and timed his activity and rest; to old age his sight and hearing did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: He then regulated his diet and kept regular hours of activity and rest; to old age his sight and hearing never failed.

sentences.zh: 既歿，安福劉球稱其學探道原，文范後世，去就出處，卓然有陶潛、徐穉之風。

translations.literal: After his death, Liu Qiu of Anfu praised his learning as probing the source of the Way, his writing as a model for later ages, and his choices in leaving and entering office as having the outstanding spirit of Tao Qian and Xu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, Liu Qiu of Anfu praised his learning as probing the source of the Way, his writing as a model for later ages, and his choices in public life as having the outstanding spirit of Tao Qian and Xu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 吳海，字朝宗，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Wu Hai, styled Chaozong, was a native of Min county.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hai, styled Chaozong, was a native of Min county.

sentences.zh: 元季以學行稱。

translations.literal: In the late Yuan he was known for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Yuan he was known for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 值四方盜起，絕意仕進。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in all quarters, he completely abandoned any wish for office.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose throughout the realm, he completely abandoned any wish for office.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，守臣欲薦諸朝，力辭免。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu, local officials wished to recommend him to the court, but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Hongwu, local officials wished to recommend him to the court, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 既而徵詣史局，復力辭。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to the History Bureau, but again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to the History Bureau, but again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「楊、墨、釋、老，聖道之賊，管、商、申、韓，治道之賊，稗官野乘，正史之賊，支詞艷說，文章之賊。

translations.literal: He once said: "Yang Zhu, Mozi, Buddhism, and Daoism are thieves of the sage's Way; Guan Zhong, Shang Yang, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei are thieves of the way of governance; unofficial histories and wild records are thieves of orthodox history; florid words and seductive discourse are thieves of good writing."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Yang Zhu, Mozi, Buddhism, and Daoism are enemies of the sage's Way; Guan Zhong, Shang Yang, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei are enemies of good governance; unofficial histories and wild records are enemies of orthodox history; florid words and seductive discourse are enemies of good writing."

sentences.zh: 上之人，宜敕通經大臣，會諸儒定其品目，頒之天下，民間非此不得輒藏，坊市不得輒粥。

translations.literal: Those above should command great ministers versed in the classics to gather the scholars and fix categories of books, promulgate them throughout the realm, forbid the people from keeping any others, and forbid markets from selling them.
translations.idiomatic: Those in authority should command great ministers versed in the classics to gather the scholars, fix categories of approved books, promulgate them throughout the realm, forbid the people from keeping any others, and forbid markets from selling them.

sentences.zh: 如是數年，學者生長不涉異聞，其於養德育才，豈曰小補。

translations.literal: If this were done for several years, scholars would grow up untouched by heterodox teachings; for nurturing virtue and cultivating talent, would this not be a small benefit?
translations.idiomatic: If this were done for several years, scholars would grow up untouched by heterodox teachings; for nurturing virtue and cultivating talent, would this not be a great benefit?

sentences.zh: 」因著書一編曰《書禍》，以發明之。

translations.literal: Accordingly he wrote a book in one fascicle called The Calamity of Books to expound this.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he wrote a book in one fascicle called The Calamity of Books to expound this view.

sentences.zh: 與永福王翰善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Wang Han of Yongfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Wang Han of Yongfu.

sentences.zh: 翰嘗仕元，海數勸之死，翰果自裁。

translations.literal: Han had once served the Yuan; Hai repeatedly urged him to die, and Han indeed took his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Han had once served the Yuan; Hai repeatedly urged him to die for principle, and Han indeed took his own life.

sentences.zh: 海教養其子偁，卒底成立。

translations.literal: Hai raised and taught Wang Han's son Cheng, and in the end brought him to full establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hai raised and educated Wang Han's son Cheng, and in the end brought him to maturity.

sentences.zh: 平居虛懷樂善，有規過者，欣然立改，因顏其齋曰聞過。

translations.literal: In ordinary life he was open-minded and delighted in goodness; when someone corrected his faults, he gladly changed at once, and therefore named his study Hearing Fault.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he was open-minded and delighted in goodness; when anyone pointed out his faults, he gladly corrected them at once, and so named his study the Hall of Hearing Fault.

sentences.zh: 為文嚴整典雅，一歸諸理，後學咸宗仰之。

translations.literal: His writing was strict, orderly, and elegant, all returning to principle; later students all looked up to him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was austere, polished, and elegant, always grounded in principle; later students all looked up to him as a model.

sentences.zh: 有《聞過齋集》行世。

translations.literal: His Collected Works of the Hearing-Fault Studio circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Works of the Hall of Hearing Fault circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 劉閔，字子賢，莆田人。

translations.literal: Liu Min, styled Zixian, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min, styled Zixian, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 生而純愨。

translations.literal: From birth he was pure and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was pure and sincere.

sentences.zh: 早孤，絕意科舉，求古聖賢禔躬訓家之法，率而行之。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he abandoned any wish for the examinations, sought the methods by which ancient sages and worthies cultivated themselves and instructed their families, and followed them in all things.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he abandoned any wish for the examinations, sought the methods by which ancient sages and worthies cultivated themselves and instructed their families, and lived by them in all things.

sentences.zh: 祖母及父喪未舉，斷酒肉，遠室家。

translations.literal: When his grandmother's and father's funerals had not yet been held, he abstained from wine and meat and kept away from his wife.
translations.idiomatic: While his grandmother's and father's funerals had not yet been held, he abstained from wine and meat and kept away from his wife.

sentences.zh: 訓鄰邑，朔望歸，則號哭殯所，如是三年。

translations.literal: He taught in a neighboring district; on the first and fifteenth of each month he returned and wailed at the coffin hall — thus for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in a neighboring district; on the first and fifteenth of each month he returned and wailed at the coffin hall — and did so for three years.

sentences.zh: 婦失愛於母，出之，獨居奉養，疾不解衣。

translations.literal: His wife lost favor with his mother, so he sent her away; he lived alone in serving his mother, and when she was ill he never removed his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife lost favor with his mother, he sent her away; he lived alone in serving his mother, and when she was ill he never removed his clothes.

sentences.zh: 母或恚怒，則整衣竟夕跪榻前。

translations.literal: When his mother was angry, he would straighten his clothes and kneel all night before her couch.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew angry, he would straighten his clothes and kneel all night before her couch.

sentences.zh: 祭享奠獻，一循古禮，鄉人莫不欽重。

translations.literal: In sacrifices, offerings, and presentations he followed ancient rites in every detail; the people of his district all held him in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In sacrifices, offerings, and presentations he followed ancient rites in every detail; the people of his district all held him in reverence.

sentences.zh: 副使羅璟立社學，構養親堂，延閔為師。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Luo Jing established a community school and built a Hall for Nurturing Parents, inviting Min as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Luo Jing established a community school and built a Hall for Nurturing Parents, inviting Min to serve as teacher.

sentences.zh: 提學僉事周孟中捐俸助養。

translations.literal: Education Intendant Zhou Mengzhong donated his salary to help support him.
translations.idiomatic: Education Intendant Zhou Mengzhong donated his salary to help support him.

sentences.zh: 知府王弼每祭廟社，必延致齋居，曰：「此人在座，私意自消。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Bi, whenever he sacrificed at the temple and altar, always invited Min to join him in fasting and purification, saying: "With this man present, private motives naturally vanish."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Prefect Wang Bi sacrificed at the temple and altar, he always invited Min to join him in fasting and purification, saying, "With this man present, private motives naturally vanish."

sentences.zh: 」置田二十余畝贍之，並受不辭。

translations.literal: He set aside more than twenty mu of fields to support him; Min accepted both without declining.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside more than twenty mu of fields to support him; Min accepted both without declining.

sentences.zh: 及母歿，即送田還官，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he immediately returned the fields to the prefecture and lived in a hut by her grave for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he immediately returned the fields to the prefecture and lived in a hut by her grave for three years.

sentences.zh: 弟婦求分產，閔闔戶自撾，婦感悟乃已。

translations.literal: His younger brother's wife asked to divide the property; Min shut the door and beat himself, and the wife, moved to understanding, desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother's wife asked to divide the property, Min shut the door and beat himself; the wife, moved to understanding, desisted.

sentences.zh: 楊黼，雲南太和人也。

translations.literal: Yang Pu was a native of Taihe in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu was a native of Taihe in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 好學，讀《五經》皆百遍。

translations.literal: He loved learning and read each of the Five Classics a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and read each of the Five Classics a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 工篆籀，好釋典。

translations.literal: He was skilled in seal and ancient script and loved Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in seal and ancient script and loved Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 或勸其應舉，笑曰：「不理性命，理外物耶？

translations.literal: When someone urged him to take the examinations, he laughed and said: "If one does not cultivate one's nature and allotted span, is one instead to cultivate external things?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to take the examinations, he laughed and said, "If one does not cultivate one's nature and allotted span, is one instead to cultivate external things?"

sentences.zh: 」庭前有大桂樹，縛板樹上，題曰桂樓。

translations.literal: Before the courtyard stood a great cassia tree; he bound planks in the tree and inscribed it the Cassia Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Before the courtyard stood a great cassia tree; he bound planks in the tree and inscribed it the Cassia Tower.

sentences.zh: 偃仰其中，歌詩自得。

translations.literal: Reclining there, he sang and composed poetry in contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Reclining there, he sang and composed poetry in contentment.

sentences.zh: 躬耕數畝供甘膬，但求親悅，不顧余也。

translations.literal: He personally farmed several mu to provide delicacies, seeking only his parents' pleasure and caring for nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: He personally farmed several mu to provide delicacies, seeking only his parents' pleasure and caring for nothing else.

sentences.zh: 注《孝經》數萬言，證群書，根性命，字皆小篆。

translations.literal: He annotated the Classic of Filial Piety in tens of thousands of words, citing many books and grounding it in nature and allotted span; every character was in small seal script.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Classic of Filial Piety in tens of thousands of words, citing many books and grounding it in nature and allotted span; every character was written in small seal script.

sentences.zh: 所用硯乾，將下樓取水，硯池忽滿，自是為常，時人咸異之。

translations.literal: When the inkstone he used ran dry and he was about to go downstairs for water, the ink pool suddenly filled; from then on this became constant, and people of the time all thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: When the inkstone he used ran dry and he was about to go downstairs for water, the ink pool suddenly filled; from then on this became constant, and people of the time all thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 父母歿，為傭營葬畢，入雞足，棲羅漢壁石窟山十餘年，壽至八十。

translations.literal: After his parents died, he hired himself out until their burial was complete, then entered Mount Jizu and dwelt at the Stone-Cave Mountain of Luohan Cliff for more than ten years; he lived to eighty.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died, he hired himself out until their burial was complete, then entered Mount Jizu and dwelt at the Stone-Cave Mountain of Luohan Cliff for more than ten years; he lived to eighty.

sentences.zh: 子遜迎歸，一日沐浴，令子孫拜，曰：「明日吾行矣。

translations.literal: His son Xun brought him home; one day he bathed, had his descendants bow, and said: "Tomorrow I depart."
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun brought him home; one day he bathed, had his descendants bow, and said, "Tomorrow I depart."

sentences.zh: 」果卒。

translations.literal: Indeed he died.
translations.idiomatic: And indeed he died.

sentences.zh: 孫一元

translations.literal: Sun Yiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yiyuan

sentences.zh: 孫一元，字太初，不知何許人，問其邑里，曰：「我秦人也。

translations.literal: Sun Yiyuan, styled Taichu — no one knew where he was from; asked about his native place, he said: "I am a man of Qin."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yiyuan, styled Taichu — no one knew where he was from; asked about his native place, he said, "I am a man of Qin."

sentences.zh: 」嘗棲太白之巔，故號太白山人。

translations.literal: He once dwelt on the summit of Mount Taibai, and therefore styled himself the Taibai Mountain Man.
translations.idiomatic: He once dwelt on the summit of Mount Taibai, and therefore styled himself the Taibai Mountain Man.

sentences.zh: 或曰安化王宗人，王坐不軌誅，故變姓名避難也。

translations.literal: Some said he was a clansman of the Prince of Anhua; the prince was executed for treason, and so he changed his name to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he was a clansman of the Prince of Anhua; the prince was executed for treason, and so he changed his name to escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 一元姿性絕人，善為詩，風儀秀朗，蹤跡奇譎，烏巾白帢，攜鐵笛鶴瓢，遍游中原，東逾齊、魯，南涉江、淮，歷荊抵吳越，所至賦詩，談神仙，論當世事，往往傾其座人。

translations.literal: Yiyuan's bearing and nature were extraordinary; he was skilled at poetry, his appearance elegant and bright, his tracks strange and uncanny. In black cap and white kerchief, carrying an iron flute and crane gourd, he traveled throughout the central plains — east beyond Qi and Lu, south crossing the Yangtze and Huai, passing through Jing to reach Wu and Yue. Wherever he went he composed poetry, spoke of immortals, and discussed affairs of the age, often overwhelming those seated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan's bearing and nature were extraordinary; he was skilled at poetry, his appearance elegant and bright, his tracks strange and uncanny. In black cap and white kerchief, carrying an iron flute and crane gourd, he traveled throughout the central plains — east beyond Qi and Lu, south across the Yangtze and Huai, passing through Jing to reach Wu and Yue. Wherever he went he composed poetry, spoke of immortals, and discussed affairs of the age, often overwhelming those seated with him.

sentences.zh: 鉛山費宏罷相，訪之杭州南屏山，值其晝寢，就臥內與語。

translations.literal: Fei Hong of Qianshan, dismissed from the chancellorship, visited him at Mount Nanping in Hangzhou; finding him asleep by day, he spoke with him inside the bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Hong of Qianshan, dismissed from the chancellorship, visited him at Mount Nanping in Hangzhou; finding him asleep by day, he spoke with him inside the bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 送之及門，了不酬答。

translations.literal: When Hong saw him to the gate, Yiyuan made no response at all.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong saw him to the gate, Yiyuan made no response at all.

sentences.zh: 宏出語人曰：「吾一生未嘗見此人。

translations.literal: Hong went out and told others: "In all my life I have never seen such a man."
translations.idiomatic: Hong went out and told others, "In all my life I have never seen such a man."

sentences.zh: 」時劉麟以知府罷歸，龍霓以僉事謝政，並客湖州，與郡人故御史陵昆善，而長興吳珫隱居好客，三人者並主於其家。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Lin had retired after dismissal as prefect, and Long Ni had left office as intendant; both were guests in Huzhou. They were friendly with the former censor Ling Kun of the prefecture, while Wu Yan of Changxing lived in seclusion and loved to host guests — the three of them all presided at his home.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Lin had retired after dismissal as prefect, and Long Ni had left office as intendant; both were guests in Huzhou. They were friendly with the former censor Ling Kun of the prefecture, while Wu Yan of Changxing lived in seclusion and loved to host guests — the three of them all presided at his home.

sentences.zh: 珫因招一元入社，稱「苕溪五隱」。

translations.literal: Yan therefore invited Yiyuan to join the society, calling them the Five Recluses of Tiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan therefore invited Yiyuan to join the society, calling them the Five Recluses of Tiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 一元買田溪上，將老焉。

translations.literal: Yiyuan bought fields by the stream, intending to grow old there.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyuan bought fields by the stream, intending to grow old there.

sentences.zh: 舉人施侃雅善一元，妻以妻妹張氏，生一女而卒，年止三十七。

translations.literal: The presented scholar Shi Kan was on excellent terms with Yiyuan and gave him his wife's younger sister, Lady Zhang, in marriage. She bore a daughter and then Yiyuan died, at only thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The presented scholar Shi Kan was on excellent terms with Yiyuan and gave him his wife's younger sister, Lady Zhang, in marriage. She bore a daughter and then Yiyuan died, at only thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 珫等葬之道場山。

translations.literal: Yan and the others buried him at Mount Daochang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the others buried him at Mount Daochang.

sentences.zh: 沈周，字啟南，長洲人。

translations.literal: Shen Zhou, styled Qinan, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhou, styled Qinan, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖澄，永樂間舉人材，不就。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was recommended for talent in the Yongle era but did not accept office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng was recommended for talent in the Yongle era but did not accept office.

sentences.zh: 所居曰西庄，日置酒款賓，人擬之顧仲瑛。

translations.literal: His dwelling was called West Village; daily he set out wine to entertain guests, and people compared him to Gu Zhongying.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling was called West Village; daily he set out wine to entertain guests, and people compared him to Gu Zhongying.

sentences.zh: 伯父貞吉，父恆吉，並抗隱。

translations.literal: His uncle Zhenji and his father Hengji both resisted office and lived in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zhenji and his father Hengji both resisted office and lived in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 構有竹居，兄弟讀書其中。

translations.literal: They built the Bamboo Dwelling, where the brothers studied together.
translations.idiomatic: They built the Bamboo Dwelling, where the brothers studied together.

sentences.zh: 工詩善畫，臧獲亦解文墨。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and painting; even the servants understood letters and brushwork.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at poetry and painting; even the servants understood letters and brushwork.

sentences.zh: 邑人陳孟賢者，陳五經繼之子也。

translations.literal: A man of the district, Chen Mengxian, was the son of Chen Jing, master of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: A man of the district, Chen Mengxian, was the son of Chen Jing, master of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 周少從之游，得其指授。

translations.literal: Zhou in youth studied under him and received his instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou in youth studied under him and received his instruction.

sentences.zh: 年十一，游南都，作百韻詩，上巡撫侍郎崔恭。

translations.literal: At eleven he traveled to the southern capital, composed a hundred-rhyme poem, and presented it to Vice Commissioner Cui Gong.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he traveled to the southern capital, composed a hundred-rhyme poem, and presented it to Vice Commissioner Cui Gong.

sentences.zh: 面試《鳳凰台賦》，援筆立就，恭大嗟異。

translations.literal: Gong tested him orally on the Rhapsody of the Phoenix Terrace; he took up the brush and finished at once, and Gong greatly marvelled.
translations.idiomatic: Gong tested him orally on the Rhapsody of the Phoenix Terrace; he took up the brush and finished at once, and Gong greatly marvelled.

sentences.zh: 及長，書無所不覽。

translations.literal: When grown, he read books of every kind.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he read books of every kind.

sentences.zh: 文摹左氏，詩擬白居易、蘇軾、陸游，字仿黃庭堅，併為世所愛重。

translations.literal: His prose modeled Zuoshi; his poetry modeled Bai Juyi, Su Shi, and Lu You; his calligraphy modeled Huang Tingjian — all were loved and esteemed by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His prose modeled Zuoshi; his poetry modeled Bai Juyi, Su Shi, and Lu You; his calligraphy modeled Huang Tingjian — all were loved and esteemed by the world.

sentences.zh: 尤工於畫，評者謂為明世第一。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at painting; critics called him the foremost of the Ming age.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled at painting; critics called him the foremost painter of the Ming age.

sentences.zh: 郡守欲薦周賢良，周筮《易》，得《遁》之九五，遂決意隱遁。

translations.literal: The prefect wished to recommend Zhou as a worthy and able man; Zhou divined with the Changes and obtained the fifth line of Dun, and therefore resolved to withdraw into seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect wished to recommend Zhou as a worthy and able man; Zhou divined with the Changes and obtained the fifth line of Dun, and therefore resolved to withdraw into seclusion.

sentences.zh: 所居有水竹亭館之勝，圖書鼎彝充牣錯列，四方名士過從無虛日，風流文彩，照映一時。

translations.literal: His dwelling had the beauty of waters, bamboos, pavilions, and halls; books, tripods, and bronzes filled and crowded every space. Eminent men from all quarters visited without a day empty; his elegant spirit and literary brilliance illuminated the age.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling had the beauty of waters, bamboos, pavilions, and halls; books, tripods, and bronzes filled every space. Eminent men from all quarters visited without a day empty; his elegant spirit and literary brilliance illuminated the age.

sentences.zh: 奉親至孝。

translations.literal: In serving his parents he was supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his parents he was supremely filial.

sentences.zh: 父歿，或勸之仕，對曰：「若不知母氏以我為命耶？

translations.literal: When his father died, some urged him to take office; he replied: "Do you not know that my mother takes me as her very life?"
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, some urged him to take office; he replied, "Do you not know that my mother takes me as her very life?"

sentences.zh: 奈何離膝下。

translations.literal: How could I leave her side?
translations.idiomatic: How could I leave her side?

sentences.zh: 」居恆厭入城市，於郭外置行窩，有事一造之。

translations.literal: He always disliked entering the city; outside the walls he set up a traveling lodge and went there only when he had business.
translations.idiomatic: He always disliked entering the city; outside the walls he set up a traveling lodge and went there only when he had business.

sentences.zh: 晚年，匿跡惟恐不深，先後巡撫王恕、彭禮咸禮敬之，欲留幕下，並以母老辭。

translations.literal: In his later years he hid his tracks, fearing they were not deep enough. Successively the grand coordinators Wang Shu and Peng Li all treated him with courtesy and wished to keep him in their staffs, but he declined each time on the grounds that his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he hid his tracks, fearing they were not deep enough. Successively the grand coordinators Wang Shu and Peng Li all treated him with courtesy and wished to keep him in their staffs, but he declined each time on the grounds that his mother was old.

sentences.zh: 有郡守征畫工繪屋壁。

translations.literal: A prefect summoned painters to decorate the walls of a building.
translations.idiomatic: A prefect summoned painters to decorate the walls of a building.

sentences.zh: 裡人疾周者，入其姓名，遂被攝。

translations.literal: A neighbor who bore Zhou ill will entered his name, and he was duly conscripted.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor who bore Zhou ill will entered his name, and he was duly conscripted.

sentences.zh: 或勸周謁貴游以免，周曰：「往役，義也，謁貴游，不更辱乎！

translations.literal: Some urged Zhou to visit powerful patrons to escape service; Zhou said: "Going to serve is a matter of duty; visiting powerful patrons — would that not be an even greater disgrace!"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Zhou to visit powerful patrons to escape service; Zhou said, "Going to serve is a matter of duty; visiting powerful patrons — would that not be an even greater disgrace!"

sentences.zh: 」卒供役而還。

translations.literal: In the end he completed the service and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he completed the service and returned.

sentences.zh: 已而守入覲，銓曹問曰：「沈先生無恙乎？

translations.literal: Later the prefect went to court; the Bureau of Appointments asked: "Is Master Shen well?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the prefect went to court; the Bureau of Appointments asked, "Is Master Shen well?"

sentences.zh: 」守不知所對，漫應曰：「無恙。

translations.literal: The prefect did not know how to answer and casually replied: "He is well."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect did not know how to answer and casually replied, "He is well."

sentences.zh: 」見內閣，李東陽曰：「沈先生有牘乎？

translations.literal: When he met the Grand Secretariat, Li Dongyang said: "Has Master Shen sent a memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: When he met the Grand Secretariat, Li Dongyang said, "Has Master Shen sent a memorial?"

sentences.zh: 」守益愕，復漫應曰：「有而未至。

translations.literal: The prefect grew even more astonished and again casually replied: "He has, but it has not yet arrived."
translations.idiomatic: The prefect grew even more astonished and again casually replied, "He has, but it has not yet arrived."

sentences.zh: 」守出，倉皇謁侍郎吳寬，問「沈先生何人？

translations.literal: When the prefect came out, he hurried to visit Vice Minister Wu Kuan and asked: "Who is Master Shen?"
translations.idiomatic: When the prefect came out, he hurried to visit Vice Minister Wu Kuan and asked, "Who is Master Shen?"

sentences.zh: 」寬備言其狀。

translations.literal: Kuan fully described his appearance and character.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan fully described his appearance and character.

sentences.zh: 詢左右，乃畫壁生也。

translations.literal: Inquiring of those around him, he learned it was the wall-painting laborer.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiring of those around him, he learned it was the wall-painting laborer.

sentences.zh: 比還，謁周舍，再拜引咎，索飯，飯之而去。

translations.literal: When he returned, he visited Zhou's home, bowed twice and accepted blame, asked for a meal, was fed, and left.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he visited Zhou's home, bowed twice and accepted blame, asked for a meal, was fed, and left.

sentences.zh: 周以母故，終身不遠游。

translations.literal: Because of his mother, Zhou never traveled far in all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his mother, Zhou never traveled far in all his life.

sentences.zh: 母年九十九而終，周亦八十矣。

translations.literal: His mother died at ninety-nine; Zhou was also eighty.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died at ninety-nine; Zhou was also eighty.

sentences.zh: 又三年，以正德四年卒。

translations.literal: Three years later, in the fourth year of Zhengde, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, in the fourth year of Zhengde, he died.

sentences.zh: 陳繼儒

translations.literal: Chen Jiru
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiru

sentences.zh: 陳繼儒，字仲醇，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Chen Jiru, styled Zhongchun, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiru, styled Zhongchun, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異，能文章，同郡徐階特器重之。

translations.literal: In youth he was exceptionally bright and could write essays; Xu Jie of the same prefecture especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was exceptionally bright and could write essays; Xu Jie of the same prefecture especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 長為諸生，與董其昌齊名。

translations.literal: Grown, he became a student and was equally famous with Dong Qichang.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he became a student and was equally famous with Dong Qichang.

sentences.zh: 太倉王錫爵招與子衡讀書支硎山。

translations.literal: Wang Xijue of Taicang invited him to study with his son Heng on Mount Zhixian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue of Taicang invited him to study with his son Heng on Mount Zhixian.

sentences.zh: 王世貞亦雅重繼儒，三吳名下士爭欲得為師友。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen also greatly esteemed Jiru; eminent men of the Three Wu regions all vied to have him as teacher or friend.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen also greatly esteemed Jiru; eminent men of the Three Wu regions all vied to have him as teacher or friend.

sentences.zh: 繼儒通明高邁，年甫二十九，取儒衣冠焚棄之。

translations.literal: Jiru was enlightened and lofty in spirit; at only twenty-nine he took his Confucian cap and robes and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiru was enlightened and lofty in spirit; at only twenty-nine he took his Confucian cap and robes and burned them.

sentences.zh: 隱居昆山之陽，構廟祀二陸，草堂數椽，焚香晏坐，意豁如也。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion on the south slope of Mount Kun, built a shrine to the two Lus, and had a thatched hall of several bays; burning incense, he sat at ease, his mind open and free.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion on the south slope of Mount Kun, built a shrine to the two Lus, and had a thatched hall of several bays; burning incense, he sat at ease, his mind open and free.

sentences.zh: 時錫山顧憲成講學東林，招之，謝弗往。

translations.literal: At the time Gu Xiancheng of Wuxi lectured at the Donglin Academy and invited him, but he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gu Xiancheng of Wuxi lectured at the Donglin Academy and invited him, but he declined and did not go.

sentences.zh: 親亡，葬神山麓，遂築室東佘山，杜門著述，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: When his parents died, he buried them at the foot of Mount Shen and then built a dwelling on East She Mountain, closed his door to write, and had the resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died, he buried them at the foot of Mount Shen and then built a dwelling on East She Mountain, closed his door to write, and resolved to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 工詩善文，短翰小詞，皆極風致，兼能繪事。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and prose; short letters and brief lyrics all reached the utmost elegance, and he could also paint.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at poetry and prose; short letters and brief lyrics all reached the utmost elegance, and he could also paint.

sentences.zh: 又博文強識，經史諸子、術伎稗官與二氏家言，靡不較核。

translations.literal: He was also broadly learned with a strong memory; classics, histories, the hundred schools, technical arts, unofficial histories, and the teachings of the two traditions — none escaped his careful examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was also broadly learned with a strong memory; classics, histories, the hundred schools, technical arts, unofficial histories, and the teachings of the two traditions — none escaped his careful examination.

sentences.zh: 或刺取瑣言僻事，詮次成書，遠近競相購寫。

translations.literal: Sometimes he gathered trivial words and obscure matters, arranged them into books, and people near and far competed to buy and copy them.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he gathered trivial words and obscure matters, arranged them into books, and people near and far competed to buy and copy them.

sentences.zh: 征請詩文者無虛日。

translations.literal: Those who summoned or requested his poetry and prose had not a day empty.
translations.idiomatic: Not a day passed without someone summoning or requesting his poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 性喜獎掖士類，屨常滿戶外，片言酬應，莫不當意去。

translations.literal: By nature he delighted in encouraging scholars; shoes often filled the space outside his door, and with a word in reply none left dissatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he delighted in encouraging scholars; shoes often filled the space outside his door, and with a word in reply none left dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 暇則與黃冠老衲窮峰泖之勝，吟嘯忘返，足跡罕入城市。

translations.literal: In leisure he joined Daoist priests and old monks to exhaust the beauties of peaks and marshes, singing and calling without thought of return; his footsteps rarely entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In leisure he joined Daoist priests and old monks to exhaust the beauties of peaks and marshes, singing and calling without thought of return; his footsteps rarely entered the city.

sentences.zh: 其昌為築來仲樓招之至。

translations.literal: Qichang built the Laizhong Tower to invite him there.
translations.idiomatic: Qichang built the Laizhong Tower to invite him there.

sentences.zh: 黃道周疏稱「志尚高雅，博學多通，不如繼儒」，其推重如此。

translations.literal: Huang Daozhou in a memorial praised "noble aspiration and elegant taste, broad learning and many accomplishments — none equal Jiru"; such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou in a memorial praised "noble aspiration and elegant taste, broad learning and many accomplishments — none equal Jiru"; such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 侍郎沈演及御史、給事中諸朝貴，先後論薦，謂繼儒道高齒茂，宜如聘吳與弼故事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Shen Yan and various court dignitaries among censors and supervising secretaries successively recommended him in memorials, saying Jiru's Way was lofty and his years advanced, and that he should be invited as in the precedent of Wu Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Shen Yan and various court dignitaries among censors and supervising secretaries successively recommended him in memorials, saying Jiru's Way was lofty and his years advanced, and that he should be invited as in the precedent of Wu Yubi.

sentences.zh: 屢奉詔征用，皆以疾辭。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he received imperial summons to office, but each time declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly he received imperial summons to office, but each time declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十二，自為遺令，纖悉畢具。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-two, having himself drawn up his final instructions in every detail.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two, having himself drawn up his final instructions in every detail.
